chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Hariri, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Qumi, who said:

Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The minimum reward for the visitor of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on the bank of the Euphrates, if he knows his right, his honor, and his guardianship, is that all of his sins, past and future, will be forgiven.

key_terms.أَبِی عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Husayn a.s.)
key_terms.بِشَطِّ الْفُرَاتِ: on the bank of the Euphrates

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn (a.s.) on the Euphrates?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) highlights the profound spiritual efficacy of Ziyarat al-Ghadir or the Euphrates visitation, emphasizing that mere recognition of Imam Husayn’s (a.s.) right (Haqq), honor, and Wilayah suffices for comprehensive forgiveness. This narration underscores the Shia theological principle that correct belief in the Imam’s authority is intrinsically linked to the expiation of sins, a concept deeply rooted in the traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt. The mention of the Euphrates specifically evokes the historical context of the Battle of Karbala, linking the physical act of pilgrimage to the metaphysical reality of the Imam’s sacrifice.
